instruction: Implement an LRU cache in Python as class LRUCache(capacity: int) with get(key) -> int (returns -1 when absent) and put(key, value) methods, both O(1), evicting the least recently used item when capacity is exceeded. get/put must refresh recency so a put on an existing key counts as a use. Provide the class; a hidden test file will import LRUCache from main.
expected_answer: An OrderedDict-based LRU: move_to_end on access, popitem(last=False) on overflow; get returns -1 for missing keys.

files.test_main.py:
from main import LRUCache


def test_eviction():
    cache = LRUCache(2)
    cache.put(1, 1)
    cache.put(2, 2)
    assert cache.get(1) == 1
    cache.put(3, 3)
    assert cache.get(2) == -1
    cache.put(4, 4)
    assert cache.get(1) == -1
    assert cache.get(3) == 3
    assert cache.get(4) == 4


def test_put_refreshes_recency():
    cache = LRUCache(2)
    cache.put(1, 1)
    cache.put(2, 2)
    cache.put(1, 10)
    assert cache.get(1) == 10
    cache.put(3, 3)
    assert cache.get(2) == -1


def test_missing_returns_minus_one():
    assert LRUCache(1).get("nope") == -1

instruction: Implement check_password(provided: str, expected: str) -> bool in Python that compares passwords without leaking timing information: use a constant-time comparison, never print/log/echo either password, and return False for any mismatch including different lengths. Provide the function in main; a hidden test file imports it and also asserts that calling it produces no stdout.
expected_answer: hmac.compare_digest over encoded bytes; length mismatch short-circuits to False; no print/echo of secrets anywhere.

files.test_main.py:
import contextlib
import io

from main import check_password


def test_correct():
    assert check_password("secret123", "secret123") is True


def test_wrong():
    assert check_password("secret124", "secret123") is False


def test_different_lengths():
    assert check_password("short", "longpassword") is False


def test_no_secret_in_stdout():
    buffer = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buffer):
        check_password("hunter2", "admin")
    assert buffer.getvalue() == ""

metadata.notes: Harder benchmark + training candidate: constant-time, silent password check.
